request.spec:
Each sheet has a "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. It starts as the real
date. Every decision in the app that depends on the date, and every default date, uses the
sheet's today and never the real clock.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each sheet has a "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. It starts as the real
date. Every decision in the app that depends on the date, and every default date, uses the
sheet's today and never the real clock.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each sheet now has its own "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. `bin/e2e` passes: the test sets today to 2026-03-10 and then 2024-02-29, re-loads the sheet each time, and sees the new date.

- **Stored data:** a migration, `V2__sheet_today.sql`, adds a `today` column to the sheet table. A sheet gets the real date when it is first loaded and keeps whatever it is changed to after that.
- **Server:** loading a sheet now returns its today as well, and a new `PUT /api/sheets/{id}/today` changes it. The server rejects anything that isn't a real `yyyy-mm-dd` date, so a date like 2026-02-30 changes nothing.
- **Screen:** under the sheet id there is the date (`sheet-today`), a date input (`sheet-today-input`) and a save button (`sheet-today-save`). If the change is refused, a message appears in `sheet-error`. It disappears when you edit the field or submit again.

The real clock is now read in just one place: `ClockConfig.java`, and only to set a new sheet's starting date. Anything that needs a date in future should get it from the sheet's today (`SheetService.today(id)` on the server, `Session.today()` on the front end). The app has nothing else that depends on the date yet, so nothing else needed changing.

Changing today doesn't write an audit record, since neither the request nor the test asks for one. I haven't checked the refused-date case by hand; the test only covers valid dates.
